# rcmake Technical Reference

> Complete, factual technical reference for `rcmake` (`0.1.0`), an independent drop-in reimplementation of CMake `4.5.1` in safe Rust.

Canonical website: https://dvgyl.github.io/rcmake/
Browser playground: https://dvgyl.github.io/rcmake/playground.html
Compatibility report: https://dvgyl.github.io/rcmake/dashboard.html
Compatibility JSON: https://dvgyl.github.io/rcmake/data/latest.json
Concise index: https://dvgyl.github.io/rcmake/llms.txt
GitHub repository: https://github.com/dvgyl/rcmake

## 1. Identity, licensing, and safety boundaries

`rcmake` is an independent reimplementation of CMake 4.5.1 written in Rust. No CMake C++ source code is copied or translated, and `rcmake` never invokes an upstream `cmake` binary at runtime. One executable provides `cmake`, `ctest`, and `cpack`. A companion executable, `rcmake-lsp`, provides Language Server Protocol support for `CMakeLists.txt` and `*.cmake` files.

`rcmake` is not affiliated with Kitware. "CMake" is a trademark of Kitware, Inc.

Safety and dependency facts:

- All 35 workspace crates in `crates/rcmake-*` enforce `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` and workspace `unsafe_code = "forbid"` in `Cargo.toml`.
- Workspace Clippy lints reject `unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `panic`, `todo`, `unimplemented`, `indexing_slicing`, `string_slice`, `iter_over_hash_type`, and direct `std` filesystem, environment, process, and clock calls inside engine crates.
- Reachable input paths return structured diagnostics instead of panicking, bounded by explicit limits in `rcmake_base::Limits` on recursion depth, macro expansion, loop iterations, regular expression steps, and file sizes.
- Some third-party Rust dependencies, such as `rustix` and `memchr`, use `unsafe` internally.
- The native `rcmake` binary statically links two C compression codecs: Zstandard (`zstd` 1.5.7 via `zstd-sys`) and XZ Utils (`liblzma` 5.8 via `liblzma-sys`). Gzip uses `flate2` with `miniz_oxide`, and bzip2 uses `libbz2-rs-sys` in Rust.
- Rust code in `crates/` and Python tools in `tools/` are dual-licensed under `MIT OR Apache-2.0`.
- `rcmake` bundles the CMake 4.5.1 `Modules/`, `Templates/`, and rendered `Help/` files verbatim under `modules/cmake-4.5/` (installed as `share/cmake-4.5/`), along with derived help/policy tables listed in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`. Those files remain under `BSD-3-Clause` with all original Kitware and contributor copyright notices preserved.

## 2. Two invocation modes (`argv[0]`)

`rcmake` selects its operating mode from the executable name (`argv[0]`):

- `cmake`, `ctest`, `cpack`: Compatibility mode. Output, diagnostics, flags, and exit codes match CMake 4.5.1, subject only to the documented intentional differences in Section 8. Native `rcmake` flags (such as `--profile` or `--hermetic`) are rejected in compatibility mode.
- `rcmake`: Native mode. Adds the persistent compiler probe cache, parallel speculative compile probes, incremental configure replay, `rcmake explain`, `--profile`, `--diagnostics=rich`, `--hermetic`, and `--fetch-lock`.
- `RCMAKE_ORACLE_MODE=1`: Forces compatibility mode even when the binary is invoked as `rcmake`.

## 3. Exact CMake 4.5.1 parity scope

### Command-line tools

- `cmake`: Configure and generate, `-P` script mode, `-E` command-line utilities (`tar`, hash commands, `cmake_ninja_dyndep`, Fortran and Qt drivers, capabilities), `--build`, `--install`, `--workflow`, `--find-package`, `--preset`, and `--sarif-output`.
- `ctest`: `CTestTestfile.cmake` evaluation, parallel test scheduling, test fixtures, resource specifications, labels, repeat modes, JUnit and dashboard XML output, `discover_tests()`, and `-S` scripts.
- `cpack`: `CPackConfig.cmake` evaluation, install staging, archive generators (`TGZ`, `TXZ`, `TZST`, `TBZ2`, `TZ`, `TAR`, `ZIP`, `7Z`, and `ZIP_*` and `7Z_*` compression variants), `External`, and macOS `DragNDrop` and `Bundle`.

### Build system generators

| Generator | Generated files | Platforms | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Ninja` | `build.ninja` | macOS, Linux, Windows | Response files, depfiles, `dyndep` for C++20 modules |
| `Ninja Multi-Config` | `build.ninja`, `build-<Config>.ninja` | macOS, Linux, Windows | One file per configuration, `CMAKE_INTDIR` rules |
| `Unix Makefiles` | `Makefile` | macOS, Linux | Recursive Makefiles, header scanning, `--output-sync` |
| `Xcode` | `project.pbxproj` | macOS | Schemes, workspace settings, XCFramework rules, `xcodebuild` command plan |
| `Visual Studio 17 2022` | `.sln`, `.vcxproj`, `.vcxproj.filters` | Windows | Stable GUIDs, MSBuild command plan |
| `Visual Studio 18 2026` | `.slnx`, `.vcxproj`, `.vcxproj.filters` | Windows | Stable GUIDs, MSBuild command plan |

### Languages and toolchains

- C: C90, C99, C11, C17, C23.
- C++: Standard C++ plus C++20 and C++23 named modules (`CXX_MODULES` file sets, P1689r5 dependency files, `CXXDependInfo.json`, `CXXModules.json`, Ninja `dyndep`, compiler module maps).
- Objective-C and Objective-C++: Apple frameworks and Mach-O `@rpath` handling.
- Fortran: Source scanning for `.mod` files and module dependency collation.
- Assembly: `ASM`, `ASM_MASM`, `ASM_NASM`.
- Windows resources: `RC`.
- Qt: `AUTOMOC`, `AUTOUIC`, and `AUTORCC`.
- CUDA (partial): One end-to-end fixture in the ecosystem lane.
- HIP (partial): Rule wiring only; no HIP toolchain test yet.
- Swift (unverified): Basic property and compile-rule wiring exists in `rcmake-resolve`, but real Swift toolchain builds are not yet verified in CI or differential suites.

### Specifications and interfaces

- Policies `CMP0000` to `CMP0226`. `CMP0000` to `CMP0065` always use NEW behavior as in CMake 4.x (`cmake_minimum_required(VERSION <x>)` below 3.5 errors unless `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM` is 3.5 or higher). `CMP0066` to `CMP0226` are the 161 policies projects can still set to OLD.
- CMake Presets schema version 13 (`CMakePresets.json` and `CMakeUserPresets.json` with `include`, inheritance, conditions, and macro expansion).
- CMake File API: `codemodel` v2.12, `cache` v2, `toolchains` v1, `cmakeFiles` v1, and `configureLog` v1.
- Common Package Specification (CPS) 0.15.0: read, validate, and write.
- SPDX 3.0.1 software bill of materials (SBOM) via `CMAKE_INSTALL_SBOM_FORMATS`.
- Instrumentation API v1 (data v1.2): queries, snippets, index files, hooks, and trace output.
- Diagnostics via `cmake_diagnostic()` and SARIF 2.1.0 (`--sarif-output`).
- `compile_commands.json` export, `install(EXPORT)`, and `GNUInstallDirs`.
- Package managers: Works with existing `vcpkg` toolchain files, Conan fixtures, `find_package()`, and `FetchContent`.

## 4. Native extensions and performance mechanisms

The extensions below apply when the binary runs as `rcmake` (native mode).

### Persistent compiler probe cache

Compiler checks (`try_compile`, `check_c_source_compiles`, `check_include_file`, `check_symbol_exists`) often dominate configure wall time. `rcmake` caches verified probe results in a content-addressed store (`rcmake-store`) shared across build directories and projects.

- Every probe runs under `JournalHost`, which records all file reads, compiler search directories, depfiles, environment reads, and child processes.
- If a probe touches unverified state, the journal marks an `ImpureReason` (`ExternalWrite`, `SharedState`, `NondeterministicInput`, `UnverifiedProcess`, `ChangedInput`, or `JournalLimit`) and refuses to store the entry.
- The probe key covers the probe recipe, toolchain, and child process environment. At lookup, every recorded input file is verified by SHA-256 content digest, including the compiler executable itself (so an in-place compiler upgrade causes a miss), clang configuration files (`clang.cfg`, `<triple>.cfg`), and the GCC `specs` file.
- The cache skips publication when environment variables that change compiler behavior in unmodeled ways are set (for example `CCC_OVERRIDE_OPTIONS`, `COMPILER_PATH`, `GCC_EXEC_PREFIX`, `LD_PRELOAD`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, and `DYLD_*`).
- Control modes via `RCMAKE_PROBE_CACHE`: `readwrite` (default), `readonly`, `verify` (compares each hit against a fresh probe and uses the fresh result; recommended for CI and release builds), or `off`. `RCMAKE_NO_PROBE_CACHE=1` or `--no-probe-cache` disables the cache.
- Default cache roots: `~/Library/Caches/rcmake` on macOS, `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/rcmake` or `~/.cache/rcmake` on Linux, and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\rcmake\cache` on Windows. Override with `RCMAKE_CACHE_DIR` or `RCMAKE_PROBE_CACHE_DIR`. Default size limit is 2 GiB (`RCMAKE_CACHE_MAX_SIZE`).
- Optional remote cache supports HTTPS endpoints (`RCMAKE_CACHE_REMOTE`) with `anonymous`, `bearer`, `header`, or `s3` authentication (`RCMAKE_CACHE_REMOTE_AUTH`), explicit opt-in for uploads (`RCMAKE_CACHE_REMOTE_WRITE=1` and `RCMAKE_CACHE_REMOTE_EXPORT_CAPTURED_OUTPUT=1`), and offline mode (`RCMAKE_OFFLINE=1`).

### Parallel speculative compiler probes

By default, `rcmake` runs up to `min(4, logical CPUs)` probes in parallel (`RCMAKE_PROBE_JOBS`, bounded to 32 jobs and capped by memory, reserving 2 GiB for configure plus 1 GiB per probe job; CMake runs probes serially).

- Speculative lookahead runs only literal compile checks: `check_include_file`, `check_c_compiler_flag`, `check_cxx_compiler_flag`, `check_symbol_exists`, and `try_compile` with `SOURCE_FROM_CONTENT`.
- Speculative workers never run `try_run` or `execute_process`.
- When evaluation reaches the real command, `rcmake` recomputes the probe key and reuses the speculative result only when the key matches and recorded evidence passes validation; otherwise it runs the probe in the foreground.
- Setting `RCMAKE_PROBE_JOBS=1` forces serial probes.

### Incremental configure replay

When reconfiguring an existing build tree after editing a file, `rcmake` re-executes edited directory regions and replays unchanged subtrees from the prior configure snapshot.

- A region replays only when its entry context (executable identity, policy and diagnostic state, configure options, generator, toolchain) and all recorded inputs match. Its recorded variable, cache, and property changes are reapplied in original order.
- Any operation without a replay contract (unverified subprocess, clock or random read, unrecorded state mutation) invalidates replay for that region.
- Replay is disabled for the entire invocation when any of these are active: a toolchain file (`--toolchain` or `CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE`, including the `vcpkg` toolchain integration), a configure preset, `-C`, `PreLoad.cmake`, `--fresh`, trace options, `--profile` or `RCMAKE_PROFILE`, `--hermetic`, `RCMAKE_PROBE_CACHE=verify`, `RCMAKE_NO_INCREMENTAL=1`, `--check-system-vars`, `--log-context`, `--debug-output`, or `--debug-find*`.

### Provenance queries (`rcmake explain`)

`rcmake explain <NAME> -B <build>` inspects where a target gets each compile option, definition, include directory, and link library (including transitive `INTERFACE` and `PUBLIC` usage chains), or where a variable gets its value across files, macros, functions, cache entries, and `-D` command-line arguments.

Examples:

```sh
rcmake explain app -B build
rcmake explain CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS -B build
rcmake explain app -B build --json
```

JSON output uses the `rcmake-explain-v1` schema.

### Configure profiling (`--profile`)

`rcmake -S . -B build -G Ninja --profile[=<dir>]` (or `RCMAKE_PROFILE=<dir>`) writes `trace.json`, `stacks.folded`, and a self-contained `flamegraph.html` into a new `run-<id>` subdirectory under `<dir>` (default: `<build>/rcmake-profile`). A `current` file in `<dir>` records the latest run directory name.

### Rich diagnostics (`--diagnostics=rich`)

In native mode, `--diagnostics=rich` (the default when stderr is a terminal, or controlled via `RCMAKE_DIAGNOSTICS=cmake|rich`) renders source spans, line gutters, and help annotations. Compatibility mode always emits CMake 4.5.1 diagnostic text.

### Hermetic configure auditing (`--hermetic`)

`--hermetic=warn` reports undeclared environment reads, file reads outside allowed roots, subprocess spawns, and network access during configure. `--hermetic=strict` rejects them with a non-zero exit code. Allowlists can be configured through `RCMAKE_HERMETIC_ALLOW_ENV`, `RCMAKE_HERMETIC_ALLOW_PATHS`, and `RCMAKE_HERMETIC_ALLOW_PROGRAMS`.

### FetchContent lockfiles and prefetch (`--fetch-lock`)

`--fetch-lock=off|auto|update|frozen` (default `auto`, lockfile `rcmake-fetch.lock` via `RCMAKE_FETCH_LOCK_FILE`) pins FetchContent archive hashes and Git commit IDs. In native online mode with lock mode active and hermetic mode off, prefetch can start downloading an already-declared `FetchContent_Declare()` source with a pinned archive hash or full Git commit ID before `FetchContent_MakeAvailable()` runs. Offline builds use `RCMAKE_FETCH_OFFLINE=1` (and optionally `RCMAKE_FETCH_GIT_READ_ONLY=1`). Compatibility mode never prefetches.

## 5. Architecture across 35 crates and the `Host` trait

`rcmake` is structured as an acyclic graph of 35 workspace crates mirroring CMake's four stages:

1. **Command line (`rcmake-cli`, `rcmake-presets`):** `argv[0]` dispatch, CLI parsing, Presets v13 loading, `Host` creation.
2. **Configure (`rcmake-syntax`, `rcmake-regex`, `rcmake-expr`, `rcmake-eval`, `rcmake-commands`, `rcmake-model`):** Raw-byte listfile parsing, independent KWSys regex engine (`rcmake-regex`, not the Rust `regex` crate), variable and `if()` evaluation, scope/policy/diagnostic handling, built-in commands, and arena-based `ProjectModel` with backtraces.
3. **Generate (`rcmake-genex`, `rcmake-resolve`, `rcmake-cxxmodules`, `rcmake-fortran`, `rcmake-gen-common`, `rcmake-gen-ninja`, `rcmake-gen-make`, `rcmake-gen-xcode`, `rcmake-gen-vs`):** Evaluates generator expressions per configuration via an acyclic `GenexHost` trait seam, resolves transitive usage requirements into `ResolvedTarget`, lowers to `BuildGraph`, and formats generator outputs plus File API, `compile_commands.json`, install scripts, CTest files, CPS, and SBOM files. Generators only format `BuildGraph`, so resolution fixes repair every generator at once.
4. **Build, test, and package (`rcmake-build`, `rcmake-ctest`, `rcmake-cpack`, `rcmake-tool-e`, `rcmake-archive`):** In-process `BuildGraph` execution for `try_compile` and build fallback, `ctest`, `cpack`, `-E` tools, and archive codecs.
5. **Storage, front ends, and verification:** `rcmake-base`, `rcmake-json`, `rcmake-diag`, `rcmake-host`, `rcmake-cps`, `rcmake-instrument`, `rcmake-store`, `rcmake-fetch`, `rcmake-api`, `rcmake-lsp`, `rcmake-wasm`, `rcmake-harness`, `rcmake-fuzz`.

### The `rcmake_host::Host` abstraction

All engine crates access files, environment variables, child processes, and clocks exclusively through `Arc<dyn Host>` (`Send + Sync`), using absolute paths without mutating process working directory or process environment (`NativeHost` snapshots the environment once and passes overlays to child processes without calling `std::env::set_var`).

Two implementations pass the shared `rcmake_host::conformance::run_all` suite:

- `NativeHost`: Real OS backend (`rustix` on Unix, job objects on Windows for process groups and timeouts).
- `PureHost`: In-memory virtual filesystem with symlinks, virtual timestamps, scripted subprocesses, and ordered output logs.

Wrapping `Host` enables deterministic unit tests, `--hermetic` auditing, `JournalHost` probe tracking, incremental replay validation, `rcmake-lsp` unsaved-buffer overlays, and WebAssembly execution without altering the evaluator core.

## 6. Language server, embedded Rust API, and WebAssembly playground

### `rcmake-lsp`

Installed alongside `rcmake` by release archives and `scripts/install.sh`, or built from source with `cargo build --locked --release -p rcmake-lsp --features eval,stdio` (`--features stdio` alone builds a lexical-only server).

- Transport: LSP over standard input and output, taking no CLI arguments.
- Capabilities: hover (showing evaluated variables, targets, and per-configuration generator expressions when built with `eval`), completion, go to definition, document symbols, semantic tokens, and indentation formatting.
- Evaluates unsaved editor buffers in memory via a read/write `Host` overlay with subprocesses denied.
- Editor setup guides exist in `crates/rcmake-lsp/README.md` for VS Code (Generic LSP Client), Neovim 0.11+ and `nvim-lspconfig`, Helix, Zed, Emacs (Eglot), and CLion / JetBrains IDEs (LSP4IJ).

### `rcmake-api`

Embeds configure (`run_configure`), `WorkspaceIndex`, provenance tracking, and `explain` (`ExplainQuery`, `render_explain_terminal`, `render_explain_json`) directly in Rust applications. Crates are consumed as Git dependencies from `https://github.com/dvgyl/rcmake` (not published on crates.io).

- Default features `native` (`rcmake-store`, `rcmake-fetch`) and `archive` (`rcmake-archive` and native codecs) can be disabled with `default-features = false` to compile cleanly for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `wasm32-wasip1` with zero native C dependencies.

### Browser WebAssembly playground

Hosted at `https://dvgyl.github.io/rcmake/playground.html`, the playground runs `crates/rcmake-wasm` compiled via `scripts/build-wasm.sh` into `site/wasm/rcmake_wasm.wasm` (`wasm32-wasip1` command module, zero `unsafe` code, zero `wasm-bindgen`) with a minimal in-browser WASI shim and no backend server.

- Configures arbitrary edited `CMakeLists.txt` and `CMakePresets.json` files on `PureHost`.
- Generates live `Ninja` and `Ninja Multi-Config` build files (`build.ninja`, `build-<Config>.ninja`).
- Displays resolved targets, diagnostics with clickable source locations, and interactive `rcmake explain` provenance trees.

## 7. Installation, drop-in aliasing, upgrade, and uninstall

Prebuilt GitHub Releases archives target:

- `aarch64-apple-darwin` (Apple Silicon macOS)
- `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`
- `aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`
- `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`

Intel macOS (`x86_64-apple-darwin`) has no prebuilt archive; build from source with `scripts/install.sh --from-source`.

### Linux and macOS

Install into `~/.local` (or `$PREFIX`) with SHA-256 verification (requires `bash`, `python3`, `curl`):

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dvgyl/rcmake/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

Install and create `cmake`, `ctest`, and `cpack` symlinks to `rcmake`:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dvgyl/rcmake/main/scripts/install.sh | bash -s -- --alias-cmake
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
```

Supported `install.sh` flags: `--version <v>`, `--from-source`, `--archive <path>`, `--alias-cmake`, `--force`, `--uninstall`. Release archives and `SHA256SUMS.txt` also include GitHub build provenance attestations verifiable via:

```sh
gh attestation verify rcmake-<version>-<target>.tar.gz --repo dvgyl/rcmake
```

The installer also writes Bash, Zsh, Fish, and PowerShell completions and the `rcmake(1)` man page under `$PREFIX/share/`.

### Windows

Install into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\rcmake` (or `-Prefix <dir>`) on PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7+:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dvgyl/rcmake/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex
```

To pass `-AliasCmake`, `-Prefix`, `-Archive`, `-Version`, `-Force`, or `-Uninstall`, download `install.ps1` and run `.\install.ps1 -AliasCmake`. Manual extraction of the Windows `.zip` archive from GitHub Releases includes `cmake.exe`, `ctest.exe`, `cpack.exe`, `rcmake.exe`, and `rcmake-lsp.exe` in `bin\` next to `share\cmake-4.5\`.

### Building from source

Requires the Rust toolchain pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` (Rust 1.99.1) and Python 3:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/dvgyl/rcmake.git
cd rcmake
scripts/install.sh --from-source
```

Or build a local staged tree under `target/stage/`:

```sh
source env/env.sh
RCMAKE_STAGE_PROFILE=release scripts/stage.sh
```

### Uninstall

Run `install.sh --uninstall` with the same `PREFIX` (or remove the extracted Windows directory and PATH entry). Uninstall does not delete cached probes or FetchContent mirrors; remove the cache directory (`~/Library/Caches/rcmake`, `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/rcmake` or `~/.cache/rcmake`, or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\rcmake\cache`) to reclaim space.

## 8. Intentional differences, scope limits, and troubleshooting

Use upstream CMake 4.5.1 if your workflow depends on any of these omitted or different behaviors:

1. **Reproducible `tar` archives:** `cmake -E tar` and CPack archive generators write uid 0 and gid 0 instead of copying host user and group IDs.
2. **No interactive front ends:** `cmake-gui` and `ccmake` are not implemented (`edit_cache` prints `No interactive CMake dialog available.`).
3. **No DAP debugger:** `cmake --debugger` prints `CMake was not built with support for --debugger`, and `cmake -E capabilities` omits `debugger`.
4. **No legacy extra generators:** CodeBlocks, CodeLite, Eclipse CDT4, Kate, and Sublime Text 2 are omitted (`extraGenerators` is empty).
5. **No CPack native installers:** `DEB`, `RPM`, `NSIS`, `WIX`, `productbuild`, and `IFW` are not implemented.
6. **Legacy and niche generators omitted:** `NMake Makefiles`, `NMake Makefiles JOM`, `MSYS Makefiles`, `MinGW Makefiles`, `Borland Makefiles`, `Watcom WMake`, `Green Hills MULTI`, `FASTBuild`, and Visual Studio 14, 15, and 16 are not implemented.
7. **`try_compile` runs in-process:** Probes execute via `rcmake-build` rather than Ninja, Make, MSBuild, or xcodebuild. `rcmake` emits the same `Change Dir:` and `Run Build Command(s):` header in `OUTPUT_VARIABLE`, while inner build-tool output lines differ and MSBuild-only or Xcode-only attributes (`CMAKE_GENERATOR_TOOLSET`, `CMAKE_XCODE_ATTRIBUTE_*`) do not apply to probes.
8. **`--version` output:** Line 1 is `cmake version 4.5.1`; line 2 is `Rcmake 0.1.0` instead of the Kitware maintainer line.
9. **Language verification limits:** Swift is parsed but toolchain builds are unverified; CUDA has one ecosystem fixture; HIP has rule wiring only.
10. **Incremental replay limits:** Disabled when a toolchain file (including `vcpkg`), configure preset, `-C`, or `PreLoad.cmake` is active.
11. **`CMAKE_STRIP` install guard:** `cmake --install --strip` writes a strip rule only when `CMAKE_STRIP` is not a CMake false value (`OFF`, `NOTFOUND`, `strip-NOTFOUND`).

### Troubleshooting

- `cmake --version` prints Kitware's line: Another `cmake` appears earlier on `PATH`. Check `type -a cmake` and move the `rcmake` `bin` directory first.
- `Could not find CMAKE_ROOT`: Keep `bin/rcmake` next to `share/cmake-4.5`, or set `RCMAKE_VENDORED_DATA_ROOT` to `share/cmake-4.5`.
- `Unknown argument --profile` (or another native flag): The binary was started as `cmake`. Invoke it as `rcmake` for native flags.
- Behavior differs from CMake 4.5.1: Retry with `RCMAKE_ORACLE_MODE=1` to isolate native extensions, then file a parity bug at `https://github.com/dvgyl/rcmake/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml`.
- Suspected stale compiler check: Run with `RCMAKE_PROBE_CACHE=verify` or `RCMAKE_NO_PROBE_CACHE=1`.
- Editor hover lacks evaluated values: Rebuild `rcmake-lsp` with `--features eval,stdio`.

## 9. Verification methodology and current status

`rcmake` is verified against the pinned CMake 4.5.1 reference binary across seven layers:

1. **Unit and integration tests:** `cargo test --workspace` on `PureHost` and `NativeHost` across Linux (`ubuntu-24.04`), macOS (`macos-15`), and Windows (`windows-2025`).
2. **Recorded CLI and script cases:** `rcmake-harness` over `conformance/cases/` checking stdout, stderr, generated files, and exit codes.
3. **Upstream `Tests/RunCMake`:** Runs 371 of 463 upstream suites on macOS arm64, 362 on Linux, and 367 on Windows (excluded suites and reasons are documented in `tools/measure/runcmake_eval.py`), including 62 core suites and 56 policy suites covering `CMP0066` to `CMP0226`.
4. **Independent black-box suite:** 20 scenarios and 679 checks (`tools/measure/independent_verify.py`) covering C, C++, Objective-C++, Fortran, presets, multi-generator builds, install trees, Mach-O and ELF RPATHs, archive listings, `ctest`, `cpack`, and File API replies.
5. **Large C++ projects (10 projects at pinned tags, reduced option sets in `conformance/corpus/large_projects.toml`):** `duckdb` v1.3.2, `opencv` 4.12.0, `vtk` v9.5.0, `qtbase` v6.8.3, `llvm-project` 20.1.8, `pytorch` v2.7.1, `kcoreaddons` v6.15.0, `boost` 1.88.0, `rclcpp` 28.1.8, and `blender` v4.5.0. L1 compares configure success and stderr; L2 also compares `CMakeCache.txt`, Ninja commands and graph edges, and File API replies for listed targets.
6. **Fuzzing, soundness, and ecosystem lanes:** Seeded generative fuzzing (not coverage-guided) across 14 input formats at 1,000,000 inputs each, 16 probe-cache invalidation and crash-recovery checks (`tools/measure/probe_cache_eval.py`), 20 mutation replay soundness checks (`tools/measure/mutation_eval.py`), silent `PATH` swap verification (`tools/measure/path_swap_eval.py`), 64-shard `vcpkg` port matrix, Conan fixtures, and Qt 6 tests.
7. **Sealed unseen holdout:** 240 repositories held sealed during development and evaluated on the frozen release binary for aggregate L2 parity.

### Current verification status (`0.1.0`)

`rcmake` does not publish estimated or unmeasured numbers. All frozen release scorecard numbers populate `site/data/latest.json` and `https://dvgyl.github.io/rcmake/dashboard.html` mechanically from one frozen `v0.1.0` release verification run. Recorded pre-freeze baselines currently on disk:

- 3-OS CI (`ubuntu-24.04`, `macos-15`, `windows-2025`) and corpus smoke: 6 of 6 jobs green pre-freeze.
- Seeded generative fuzzing: 14,000,000 inputs across 14 targets, 0 failures (commit `d4356df`, `2026-11-25`).
- WebAssembly and WASI checks (`wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `wasm32-wasip1`): 6 of 6 checks passed (commit `c583dc2`, `2026-11-25`).

Benchmark methodology (published after the frozen idle release run):

- Cold configure (`tools/measure/bench_eval.py`): Synthetic 500-library C project, new build tree, empty private probe store, inherited `RCMAKE_*` variables cleared, median of N runs (with `--probe-jobs 1` available to isolate serial probes).
- New build tree with shared probe cache (`tools/measure/bench_configure.py`, `tools/measure/bench_giants.py`): Geometric mean speedup over CMake 4.5.1 in a new build tree (CMake has no cross-tree probe cache; `bench_eval.py` also reports same-tree rerun times where CMake skips cached checks).
- Leaf edit reconfigure: p95 wall time after editing one file (default edit changes no targets; `--leaf-edit compile-definition` adds a compile definition to the edited directory).

## 10. Direct answers to common developer questions

### What is a faster drop-in CMake replacement written in Rust?

`rcmake` is an independent drop-in reimplementation of CMake 4.5.1 in safe Rust. It reads existing `CMakeLists.txt` files, Presets v13, and caches without requiring a migration to a new build language, and accelerates configures in native mode using a verified cross-project compiler probe cache, parallel speculative compile probes, and incremental configure replay.

### Does rcmake work with existing CMakeLists.txt, Ninja, Xcode, Visual Studio, vcpkg, and Conan?

Yes. `rcmake` runs existing `CMakeLists.txt` files and bundles the CMake 4.5.1 standard `Modules/` and `Templates/`. It generates `Ninja`, `Ninja Multi-Config`, `Unix Makefiles`, `Xcode` (macOS), and `Visual Studio 17 2022` and `18 2026` (Windows) build trees, and supports `vcpkg` toolchain files and Conan fixtures (note that incremental replay disables itself when a toolchain file such as `vcpkg` is active, while compatibility configure and the probe cache continue to work).

### How do I verify whether rcmake matches CMake 4.5.1 on my project?

Install `rcmake`, run your build with `RCMAKE_ORACLE_MODE=1` or via the `cmake` alias to stay in strict CMake 4.5.1 compatibility mode, and compare the generated `CMakeCache.txt`, Ninja commands, or File API replies. For CI and release builds using native mode, set `RCMAKE_PROBE_CACHE=verify` to check every probe cache hit against a fresh probe.

### Can I run CMake in WebAssembly or in a browser?

Yes. `rcmake-api` with `default-features = false` compiles for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` and `wasm32-wasip1` on the in-memory `PureHost`. The live browser playground at `https://dvgyl.github.io/rcmake/playground.html` runs the compiled `rcmake_wasm.wasm` engine client-side to configure projects, generate `build.ninja`, report diagnostics, and run `rcmake explain`.
